brief: Carlyle argues AI capex has moved from an earnings story to a capital-markets one. Semiconductor net income growth went from a 9-10% trend to 22% after ChatGPT and above 150% over the past year, and hyperscalers are shifting from net providers of liquidity to net consumers: US corporate net savings are down 86% versus the same point in the prior cycle. Cash flow no longer covers intended spending, so over 80% of AI capex through 2030 needs external financing, and AI-related financing should exceed $500bn in 2026, more than double 2025. That financing competes with government borrowing for a shrinking savings pool, which Carlyle ties to one-year rates rising 130bp, 50bp above SOFR, since forwards implied a 2.75% terminal rate six months ago; AI itself, the note argues, is a reason rates stay above 5%, not that AI happens despite them. GS separately flags equity concentration: the top 10 stocks should generate over two-thirds of S&P 500 earnings growth this quarter, GS's S&P-ex-AI basket fell from about 3,300 in August to about 3,075, and hedge funds bought TMT in September while selling nearly every other sector. A quoted desk view counters that compute demand is real.
